clue.text: What may restrict Polly's walk in London

definitions.text: What may restrict Polly's walk in London

parts.words: What may restrict Polly's walk in London
parts.note: Polly is the stock name for a pet parrot, and the thing that confines one also names a street beside St James's Park in London

explanation.surface: A question about what limits where a woman called Polly can stroll in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Birdcage Walk is a road in Westminster, London, running beside St James's Park; Polly is the traditional name for a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet parrot is kept in a wire cage, and Birdcage Walk is a well-known London street.

clue.text: White powder in piece of cloth vehicle carries around

indicators.note: carries around means the cloth word is wrapped about the vehicle word

parts.note: a bib is a piece of cloth worn under the chin
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: White dust found in a piece of fabric that a vehicle carries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only links the definition to the wordplay; 'carries around' tells you the cloth is wrapped round the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium bicarbonate, used in baking, is a white powder; the answer is its short name.

clue.text: Speak in ceremony outside city

indicators.note: outside means the ceremony word goes round the city abbreviation

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Speaking at a ceremony held outside the city.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode district of the City of London, its financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to say aloud from memory, a way to speak.

clue.text: Girl dressed inadequately, artist

indicators.note: inadequately means the dressed word falls short of its last letter

parts.note: clad means dressed
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A girl wearing too little, and she is a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAD lacks its final D; RA is a member of the Royal Academy.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Sentimentality over attractive person not all that wonderful

indicators.note: over means placed above in a down answer

parts.note: goo is slang for gushing sentimentality
a dish is slang for a good-looking person

explanation.surface: Gushing over a good-looking person who is, frankly, merely okay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fairly good is only moderately pleasing, not marvellous.

clue.text: Exclamation in school when there's roast

indicators.note: in tells us the exclamation is placed inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone shouts in surprise at school on the day a roast is served.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise, as in 'Cor blimey!'.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast something is to heat it fiercely, which is what scorching means; both are verbs of burning heat.

clue.text: Dog followed and cut short

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to tail is to follow

explanation.surface: A dog was tracked and had its tail docked.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtailed means shortened or reduced.

clue.text: Tree in Burma exceptionally brown

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests an unusual arrangement of the country's letters

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: A tree in Myanmar that is unusually brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' rearranges BURMA into RAMBU.
explanation.definitionFit: This Southeast Asian tree bears a red hairy fruit related to the lychee.

clue.text: She and I organised gallery stall

indicators.note: organised means the letters of the two words are arranged anew

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Two people arrange a stand at an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges SHE and I into HESI; the Tate is a group of British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to delay or hold back from acting, as when one hesitates.

clue.text: Heartlessly capture many a whale

indicators.note: heartlessly means the central letter of the word for capture is removed

parts.note: to capture is to catch
many means a lot

explanation.surface: Someone callously sets out to catch a lot of whales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' removes T, the middle letter of CATCH, leaving CACH.
explanation.definitionFit: The sperm whale is also known by this older name, so it is a type of whale.

clue.text: Not much food and drink consumed by American broadcasters

indicators.note: consumed by puts the drink inside the letters of the broadcaster, as if swallowed

parts.note: CBS is a major American television network
rum is a drink

explanation.surface: US television networks devour food and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumbs are tiny scraps of bread or cake, so very little to eat.

clue.text: Pollution with sulphur getting elder statesman upset

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

indicators.note: upset in a down answer means turned upside down, so read from bottom up

parts.note: GOM is Grand Old Man, a title for a veteran statesman, first Gladstone

explanation.surface: A veteran politician is upset about sulphurous pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: GOM, the Grand Old Man, was Gladstone's nickname; 'upset' turns it to MOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend of smoke and fog forms a polluting haze over cities.

clue.text: I must rail about undue emphasis on ceremony

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A person vows to protest against making too much of formal ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of I MUST RAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritualism is excessive devotion to rites and formal practices in worship.

clue.text: Only half spoil child? No

indicators.note: only half means the word for spoil is cut down to its first half

parts.note: to adulterate is to spoil by adding impurities

explanation.surface: A parent weighs whether spoiling a child only halfway is acceptable, and decides no.
explanation.walkthrough: ADULTERATE (spoil, ten letters) loses its second half, ERATE, leaving the first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up person is precisely someone who is not a child, so 'child? No' points to that.

clue.text: Institution with church highly decorated

parts.note: RI stands for the Royal Institution

explanation.surface: An establishment with an ornate church.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Institution is a London scientific body, abbreviated RI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich decoration is lavish and ornate, so highly decorated fits.

clue.text: I troubled mine aunt before very long

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred around

explanation.surface: A nephew admits upsetting his aunt shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges I MINE AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening shortly will occur soon.

clue.text: Good to everyone, little creature being brave

parts.note: all means everyone
an ant is a small insect

explanation.surface: A tiny animal showing courage and kindness toward all.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant person is courageous and chivalrous.

clue.text: Disease got by daughter tucking into pie mice fouled up

indicators.note: tucking into means the daughter abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
fouled up means messed about, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A girl catches an illness from eating a pie that mice have spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fouled up' rearranges PIE MICE into EPIEMIC, and 'tucking into' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread outbreak of infectious illness.

clue.text: Man behind bars?

parts.note: suggests a prisoner, but the bars are those of a pub counter

explanation.definitionFit: A pub landlord works behind the bar serving drinks.

clue.text: Natural covering fruit gets with time

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A fruit develops a natural skin as it ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's feathers are its natural coat.

clue.text: Some see a star and point

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people looking up see a star and point at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'and point' as the definition, but 'and' is only a link; the definition is 'point', a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: North, south, east and west are the compass points.

clue.text: Caused to be insane before end of life

parts.note: mad means insane

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word life

explanation.surface: Being driven mad before the end of one's life.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made something happen is to have caused it.

clue.text: Academic club first appearing in old kingdom

indicators.note: first appearing means the club word comes before the academic word

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A university club's opening meeting held in an ancient land.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great's ancient realm in northern Greece.

clue.text: Settle three-quarters of the plan at the end of the month

indicators.note: at the end of puts the shortened plan after the month

parts.note: DEC is December, the last month

indicators.note: three-quarters of keeps three of the four letters of the plan word

parts.note: an idea is a plan

explanation.surface: Agreeing most of a scheme at month's end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-quarters of' drops the plan word's final letter; 'at the end of' puts that shortened word after the month.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a question is to resolve or make up one's mind about it.

clue.text: Saint — one died, being this

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A saint who died by martyrdom, as St Stephen was.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: St Stephen, the first martyr, died by being pelted with rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Early martyrs such as St Stephen were killed by having rocks thrown at them.

clue.text: Indian state in which Derek's given greeting

parts.note: Del is a short form of the name Derek
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A man called Derek is welcomed somewhere in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Capital Territory of this name is a state-level region of India.

clue.text: A crowd outwardly ecstatic in religious ceremony

indicators.note: outwardly means the word for ecstatic is placed around the other letters

parts.note: sent is an old slang word for ecstatic, carried away
to cram is to crowd

explanation.surface: Worshippers packed together, visibly overjoyed at a church rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' is dated slang for thrilled or carried away, and 'outwardly' makes it the outer shell of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism and Communion are examples of these Christian rites.

clue.text: Like a top event restricted by fundmentalists

indicators.note: restricted by means held within the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A top event confined by religious hardliners.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue misspells 'fundamentalists', but the hidden run is unaffected.
explanation.definitionFit: The best celebrities form an elite group, and an event full of them is described this way.

clue.text: Model given ridicule at university

parts.note: to mock is to ridicule
up means in residence at university, as in going up to Oxford

explanation.surface: A fashion model is mocked while at college.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at university when in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock-up is a full-size model or prototype of something.

clue.text: Extra sum at school?

definitions.meaning: something extra is an added item
a sum in a school maths lesson where numbers are totted up

explanation.definitionFit: Something added on is an extra, and adding numbers is one of the basic sums taught in school.

clue.text: Isn't queen able to move at a gentle pace?

parts.note: isn't able gives can't, with able completing the phrase after the queen
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Asking whether the queen cannot ride slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'isn't able' is split by 'queen': its first word gives the contraction and 'able' completes it; ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse moving at a canter goes faster than a trot but slower than a gallop.

clue.text: Like a football match using the entire pitch throughout

definitions.text: Like a football match using the entire pitch
definitions.meaning: a lively game where play swings from one goal to the other
throughout means over the whole length

explanation.definitionFit: A game swinging between both goals is described this way, and the phrase also means over the full length.
